headline: DPP technical resources, CSRD assurance consultation, and proposed CBAM expansion
summary: The European Commission released technical guidance for Digital Product Passport registry integration and opened a consultation on CSRD limited assurance standards. Meanwhile, rules were adopted for CBAM carbon cost deductions alongside reported proposals to extend CBAM to downstream steel and aluminium products.

items.title: Commission releases Digital Product Passport registry technical documentation
items.what: The European Commission published technical documentation and six technical resources to support companies connecting to the Digital Product Passport registry.
items.meaning: As a manufacturer and importer of battery-powered tools, these technical specifications provide the exact requirements needed to prepare data architecture for future product passports.
items.action: Pass technical resources to IT and compliance teams to evaluate DPP system architecture requirements.

sources.title: EU Publishes Digital Product Passport Registry Documentation
Commission publishes six technical resources for companies connecting to the digital product passport registry

items.title: Commission consults on CSRD limited assurance standards
items.what: The European Commission launched a consultation on limited assurance standards under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive.
items.meaning: Directly impacts your CSRD reporting requirements, clarifying how independent auditors will verify reported sustainability metrics.
items.action: Review consultation draft to align Chinese supplier data collection with expected auditor verification standards.

sources.title: EU CSRD: Commission consults on limited assurance standards, Julia Voskoboinikova

items.title: EU adopts CBAM deduction rules and considers downstream extension
items.what: The EU finalized rules for deducting third-country carbon costs, recognizing China's ETS. Reports also indicate a proposed extension to 180 downstream steel and aluminium products.
items.meaning: Finished tools are currently exempt, but proposed downstream scope expansion could cover imported hardware components. Deductions for Chinese ETS payments could offset future carbon costs.
items.action: Identify which Chinese suppliers pay into China's ETS and track proposed downstream product lists.

sources.title: EU Recognizes China’s Carbon Market for Border Levy Deductions

EU sets rules for deducting third-country carbon costs under CBAM, recognizes Turkey’s ETS

items.title: Corrigendum published for EU Machinery Regulation
items.what: An official corrigendum to the EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 was published in the Official Journal.
items.meaning: Provides legal clarity ahead of the regulation taking effect and replacing the old Machinery Directive in January 2027.
items.action: Verify technical compliance documentation against the corrected legal text.
